Hi Ahmad,

It was easier to review everything on your pdf on my computer. Doug mentioned that it may be worth changing the order of operations for the stump trimming and killing to reflect killing the stump after it has been trimmed to help avoid them accidentally cutting off the poisoned portion of the stump. It may also be worth putting some sort of catch-all section in case there were any stumps that need to be trimmed that we couldn't observe from the bottom of the slope.

Below is a draft of the letter I'm going to send to the GC on Monday. I think Doug is going to try to give Dave a call to discuss. We want to make sure what we're sending over is in line with whatever you guys end up sending.

-----
Hi Alfonso,

I stopped by the job site last Thursday afternoon, and it looked like Greenleaf was making some good progress on addressing some of the concerns we discussed at our meeting earlier this week. The gentleman who was covering for you mentioned that Greenleaf was going to be done by the end of the day on Friday. I want to make sure we're all on the same page regarding what needs to be done to the stumps prior to Tecco Net installation as them finishing that quickly didn't look plausible to me based on where they were at when I left the site.

All stumps that will be covered in Tecco net need to be cut to (or slightly beneath) the existing grade of the slope and then killed. If we tension the Tecco net over a stump that has been killed that is above the existing grade of the slope, any stump decay that may occur will lead to voids in the net that will result in the net losing tension over time. If the stumps are cut to be level with (or slightly beneath) the existing slope, the net will stay tight against the slope even if the dead stumps start to decay.

Can you please confirm that what I've written above is in line with the work that Greenleaf is currently executing? If yes, were they able to complete that work last week?

I also want to follow up on the two other minor issues that were brought up at the meeting last Tuesday.
